to content\nDEPARTMENTS & SERVICES\nRESOURCES\nABOUT\nCONTACT\nHOW DO I\n/\nABOUT\nABOUT THE CLERK\nABOUT JAMES M. SWISHER, JR.\n\nAppointed in August, 2020 by Governor Ron DeSantis, James M. Swisher, Jr. serves as Clerk of Circuit Court & Comptroller for Columbia County. In this role, he oversees all funds of the county, manages a staff of 35, and is responsible for more than 1,000 constitutional and regulatory duties.\n\nSwisher brings significant leadership and management experience to his role as Clerk of the Courts and Comptroller. In addition to serving most recently as the Director of the Public Safety Training Center at Florida Gateway College, he also brings years of experience working within the judiciary system in many different capacities. This includes his work as a deputy sheriff, public defender investigator, and surety agent intern.\n\nSwisher is a lifelong resident of Columbia County who graduated in 2004 from the University of Florida with his Bachelor’s Degree in Criminology. He has been a public servant for most of his adult life; becoming your Clerk of Circuit Court was a natural progression of his public service.\n\nDUITES OF THE CLERK\nAs Clerk of the Courts\n\nThe Clerk of Court’s Office is a multifaceted organization that performs a wide range of record-keeping and financial management services for the judicial system, the Board of County Commissioners, and most importantly, the citizens of Columbia County.\n\nThis office gives support to judges in court proceedings; secures evidence, ensures that the integrity of court files is protected, and assists law enforcement and crime victims. The Clerk maintains custody of all court records and of all related pleadings filed.\n\nSwisher’s staff coordinates jury duty, record retention, record destruction, and manages the historical archives. Swisher and his staff collect and distribute state and county fines, fees, court costs, registries, and service charges. Essentially, everything in the judicial system begins and ends with the Clerk’s Office services in some way.\n\nAs Recorder\n\nAs Recorder, the Clerk records final judgments, mortgages, and deeds, and maintains the official records of Columbia County, ensuring that their integrity is protected. Additionally, the Clerk provides passport and marriage license services and submits information to the Bureau of Vital Statistics.\n\nAs Clerk & Accountant of the Board of County Commissioners\n\nThe Clerk attends all Board meetings, records the proceedings, keeps minutes, maintains county financial records, and prepares financial reports.\n\nAs Chief Financial Officer\n\nSwisher is the custodian of all county funds and is also the county auditor. The Clerk performs a wide variety of services, which include maintenance of financial records, preparing reports, investing county funds, pre-auditing of county expenditures, and maintenance of official records of the Board of County Commissioners. In this capacity, the Clerk ensures that all expenditures of county funds are authorized by law.\n\nAs Your Elected Official\n\nSwisher delivers quality service in the most cost-effective manner, serves as a trustee in handling collection and disbursement of funding for numerous agencies, and serves as a “watchdog” for the citizens of Columbia County to ensure funds expended are only for a public purpose and for the benefit of the public as a whole.\n\nEXPLORE THIS SECTION\nAbout the Clerk\nNews & Announcements\nfollow us on facebook link opens in a new tab\nCONTACT US\n(386) to content\nDEPARTMENTS & SERVICES\nRESOURCES\nABOUT\nCONTACT\nHOW DO I\n/\nCOURT SERVICES\nCIRCUIT & COUNTY CIVIL\nCIRCUIT CIVIL\n\nCircuit Civil has jurisdiction over civil actions in which the matter in controversy exceeds the sum of $15,000.00, all cases in equity, actions involving the title and boundaries of real property, injunctions, and all civil matters not within the jurisdiction of the county court.\n\nThe Circuit Civil Department maintains the records and documentation for cases involving lawsuits greater than $50,000.01. Other types of cases handled by Circuit Civil are mortgage and lien foreclosure, medical and professional malpractice, auto negligence, contract indebtedness, personal injury, and eminent domain.\n\nThe public may view most Circuit Civil case files unless the case has been sealed. In which case, it cannot be viewed without a court order. If you require legal advice or need information not provided here, you may need to consult an attorney licensed in the State of Florida or some other qualified source, such as the Florida Bar or the Law Library.\n\nHelpful Links\nFlorida Bar Rules of Civil Procedure\nFlorida Bar Lawyers Referral Service\nCOUNTY CIVIL\n\nCounty Civil has jurisdiction over civil actions in which the matter in controversy does not exceed the sum of $15,000.00. Claims of more than $5,000.00 but less than $15,000.00 are categorized as county civil actions.\n\nThe County Civil Department maintains the records and documentation for cases involving eviction lawsuits, small claims, and other civil lawsuits less than $50,000.00 to include car repair disputes, release of personal property, and payment information for judgments.\n\nHelpful Links\nFlorida Bar Rules of Civil Procedure\nFlorida Bar Consumer Information\nFlorida Bar Lawyers Referral Service\nFlorida Bar Tenant and Landlord Rights\nFlorida PIRG Renters Rights Online Handbook\nJudgement Lien
